      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

blocks.text:
# gh-1596: [GOAL] POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard — setup.sh completes under curl | sh on dash/busybox/bash (fixes #1596 crash)

## Description

## Goal — POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard (v1, converted from bug report)
One sentence: **`curl -fsSL https://fa1.dev/setup.sh | sh` completes the full first-run wizard and writes a working `~/.fah/config.yaml` under every mainstream POSIX sh — dash, busybox ash, bash — not only bash.**

Today `site/setup.sh` is bash-only: 7 uses of the bash builtin `printf -v`. Under `curl | sh` the shebang is ignored — whatever `sh` resolves to executes the script — and on Ubuntu 24.04 (sh = dash) the wizard aborts at the first prompt: `printf: Illegal option -v`. `.fah` is never created. Reported by an external user (khoser); this is the first-run experience for every new Linux user.

## Why this framing
- The fix lands in the **generator pipeline**, not the artifact: `site/install-config.yaml` + `site/setup.sh.template` → `scripts/gen_installers.dart` → `site/setup.sh` (`DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` header). A hand-patch of `site/setup.sh` regresses on the next release.
- Retracted framing: "add/fix the bash shebang" — under `curl | sh` a shebang is dead text; the script must be valid for whatever shell the pipe feeds. Never revisit.
- The wizard's interactive-stdin design is already correct (`read … < /dev/tty`, non-TTY guard at the top) — this card changes **nothing** about the UX, only the shell dialect.

## Architecture
```
site/install-config.yaml ─┐
site/setup.sh.template ───┴─> scripts/gen_installers.dart ──> site/setup.sh  (curl | sh target)
                                                            └> site/install.sh, install.bat/ps1
```
Invariants:
- **I1 (dialect):** every `sh`-targeted emitted script parses and runs under dash, busybox ash, and bash. POSIX subset only: no `printf -v`, no `[[ ]]`, no arrays, no `local -a`, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no `${var,,}`, no `=~`.
- **I2 (single source):** emitted `site/setup.sh` is byte-identical to a fresh regeneration (existing pin/selftest guards keep enforcing this).
- **I3 (UX parity):** prompt texts, provider menu, hidden key entry (`read -rs < /dev/tty`), and the non-TTY degradation path behave identically on bash and dash.

## Capability surface (what the wizard must do → portability shape)
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt helpers (`ask`, `ask_hidden`, `confirm`) | `printf -v` assignment (bash-only) | POSIX assignment via command substitution (`var=$(…)`) with exit-code propagation |
| Interactive stdin | `read -r < /dev/tty` (correct) | unchanged |
| Non-TTY path | guard at line 143, clear message | unchanged + IT-covered |
| Config write | `~/.fah/config.yaml` | unchanged (E3 pins no-clobber) |
| CI portability guard | none | **core**: dash + busybox smoke jobs |
| `shellcheck --shell=sh` over emitted sh | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Non-interactive env setup (`FA_SETUP_PROVIDER=…`) | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Rewrite wizard in another language / compiled helper | — | **excluded**: 400 lines of POSIX sh is the right tool; a binary bootstrap adds supply-chain surface for zero UX gain |
| Re-exec into bash from the piped script | — | **excluded**: impossible without writing a temp file from remote code — new attack surface; removing bashisms is strictly simpler |

### Platform facts (pinned, each with a test)
- **dash** (Ubuntu `sh`, Debian): `printf` has no `-v` → the #1596 crash. Negative test: dash run of the old script fails at line 74; positive: new script completes.
- **busybox ash** (Alpine, slim containers): same; also strict about `local` outside functions. Smoke-covered.
- **macOS `sh`** = bash 3.2 POSIX mode: *accepts* `printf -v` (bash builtin quirk) — that's why the bug never fired on macOS. Positive test only (no macOS regression possible from this fix).
- **`/dev/tty`** exists in interactive sessions, absent in non-interactive CI pipes → the existing non-TTY guard is the degradation path (IT-asserted).

### Security (remote `curl | sh` + typed secrets)
- Threat: the wizard collects a **provider API key**. Invariants: the key is read via `read -rs < /dev/tty` (never echoed), lands **only** in `~/.fah/config.yaml`, never appears in argv/`ps` output, transcripts, or logs; the config write keeps current file-mode behavior.
- The POSIX rewrite must not "simplify" hidden input into visible echo or pass the key through `printf` argv in a way `ps` can catch (assign via `read`, not `var=$(… key on the command line)`).
- Supply chain: served over HTTPS from fa1.dev; existing `check_install_pin.sh` / `installer_verify_selftest.sh` guards stay. Checksum infrastructure = separate card (out of scope).

## Freshness audit (fresh main `92e939246`, 2026-10-14)
The dialect bug is not the only problem — the wizard's data is stale. Verified against fresh main; all `site/` files are byte-identical to the generator output (no artifact drift), so every finding below lives in the **source** (`site/install-config.yaml` + template) and ships on every fresh download:

| Surface | Wizard offers | fa reality (origin/main) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | 5: openrouter, anthropic, google, openai, custom | **12** in `provider_catalog.dart`: + copilot, zai, kimi, codemie, dial, minimax, chatgpt, aiin | **stale** |
| Approval modes | 3: yolo, write, always-ask | **4**: + `autopilot` (`kAutopilotLabel`, formerly `unattended`) | **stale** |
| Model presets | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 (recommended)`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` | current catalog defaults | **stale** |
| Agent modes | code, architect, review | `builtInAgentModes` = default(code), architect, review | ✓ current |
| Config keys written | provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode/allowedTools | all live in `settings_registry` (`yamlKeys`) | ✓ current |
| Interactive stdin (`read < /dev/tty`), non-TTY guard | as designed | unchanged on main | ✓ current |

Provider surface is actively moving upstream (gh-1554 scoped timeouts, gh-1570 ProviderModelBinding) — another reason the wizard's provider data must be **generated from the live catalog**, not hand-maintained in yaml.

### Addition to the fix (same card)
- **AC6** — the wizard's provider list, approval-mode list, and model presets are **generated from `provider_catalog.dart`** (gen_installers reads the catalog or a checked-in snapshot with a drift test): provider menu names == catalog names, approval menu = always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot, presets = current recommended defaults. A catalog change without regeneration fails `UT-2` (golden drift, extended to the data sections).
- Provider menu ordering: keep openrouter first (recommended), then the rest by catalog order; `custom` stays last.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `site/setup.sh.template` contains zero POSIX-violating constructs (automated scan: `printf -v`, `[[`, `read -p`, arrays, `${var,,}`, `=~`); regenerated `site/setup.sh` identical to the scan-clean template. Hook: `gen_installers` golden test + a new template lint.
- **AC2** — Piped wizard (`curl -fsSL … | sh` equivalent: `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'`) with scripted `/dev/tty` answers picks Custom (option 5), accepts endpoint+key, writes a valid `~/.fah/config.yaml`, exits 0 — under **dash**, **busybox ash**, and **bash**. Hook: IT pty harness.
- **AC3** — The hidden API key never appears in the captured transcript of the IT runs (byte-scan the fixture for the key literal) and `~/.fah/config.yaml` contains it exactly once.
- **AC4** — Non-TTY run prints the existing clear guidance and exits non-zero without writing `.fah` (parity with today's guard).
- **AC5** — `bash site/setup.sh` (direct, non-piped) behavior is unchanged (existing UX preserved; no prompt-text drift).

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-1` — template lint: forbidden-construct scan (AC1). Pure grep/dart, no IO.
- `UT-2` — golden drift: emitted `site/setup.sh` == regeneration from template+yaml (AC1; extends the existing selftest).
- `IT-1` — dash pty run, full wizard, option 5 Custom, fixture config asserted (AC2, AC3).
- `IT-2` — busybox ash pty run, same fixture (AC2).
- `IT-3`…

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

blocks.text:
# gh-1596: [GOAL] POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard — setup.sh completes under curl | sh on dash/busybox/bash (fixes #1596 crash)

## Description

## Goal — POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard (v1, converted from bug report)
One sentence: **`curl -fsSL https://fa1.dev/setup.sh | sh` completes the full first-run wizard and writes a working `~/.fah/config.yaml` under every mainstream POSIX sh — dash, busybox ash, bash — not only bash.**

Today `site/setup.sh` is bash-only: 7 uses of the bash builtin `printf -v`. Under `curl | sh` the shebang is ignored — whatever `sh` resolves to executes the script — and on Ubuntu 24.04 (sh = dash) the wizard aborts at the first prompt: `printf: Illegal option -v`. `.fah` is never created. Reported by an external user (khoser); this is the first-run experience for every new Linux user.

## Why this framing
- The fix lands in the **generator pipeline**, not the artifact: `site/install-config.yaml` + `site/setup.sh.template` → `scripts/gen_installers.dart` → `site/setup.sh` (`DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` header). A hand-patch of `site/setup.sh` regresses on the next release.
- Retracted framing: "add/fix the bash shebang" — under `curl | sh` a shebang is dead text; the script must be valid for whatever shell the pipe feeds. Never revisit.
- The wizard's interactive-stdin design is already correct (`read … < /dev/tty`, non-TTY guard at the top) — this card changes **nothing** about the UX, only the shell dialect.

## Architecture
```
site/install-config.yaml ─┐
site/setup.sh.template ───┴─> scripts/gen_installers.dart ──> site/setup.sh  (curl | sh target)
                                                            └> site/install.sh, install.bat/ps1
```
Invariants:
- **I1 (dialect):** every `sh`-targeted emitted script parses and runs under dash, busybox ash, and bash. POSIX subset only: no `printf -v`, no `[[ ]]`, no arrays, no `local -a`, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no `${var,,}`, no `=~`.
- **I2 (single source):** emitted `site/setup.sh` is byte-identical to a fresh regeneration (existing pin/selftest guards keep enforcing this).
- **I3 (UX parity):** prompt texts, provider menu, hidden key entry (`read -rs < /dev/tty`), and the non-TTY degradation path behave identically on bash and dash.

## Capability surface (what the wizard must do → portability shape)
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt helpers (`ask`, `ask_hidden`, `confirm`) | `printf -v` assignment (bash-only) | POSIX assignment via command substitution (`var=$(…)`) with exit-code propagation |
| Interactive stdin | `read -r < /dev/tty` (correct) | unchanged |
| Non-TTY path | guard at line 143, clear message | unchanged + IT-covered |
| Config write | `~/.fah/config.yaml` | unchanged (E3 pins no-clobber) |
| CI portability guard | none | **core**: dash + busybox smoke jobs |
| `shellcheck --shell=sh` over emitted sh | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Non-interactive env setup (`FA_SETUP_PROVIDER=…`) | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Rewrite wizard in another language / compiled helper | — | **excluded**: 400 lines of POSIX sh is the right tool; a binary bootstrap adds supply-chain surface for zero UX gain |
| Re-exec into bash from the piped script | — | **excluded**: impossible without writing a temp file from remote code — new attack surface; removing bashisms is strictly simpler |

### Platform facts (pinned, each with a test)
- **dash** (Ubuntu `sh`, Debian): `printf` has no `-v` → the #1596 crash. Negative test: dash run of the old script fails at line 74; positive: new script completes.
- **busybox ash** (Alpine, slim containers): same; also strict about `local` outside functions. Smoke-covered.
- **macOS `sh`** = bash 3.2 POSIX mode: *accepts* `printf -v` (bash builtin quirk) — that's why the bug never fired on macOS. Positive test only (no macOS regression possible from this fix).
- **`/dev/tty`** exists in interactive sessions, absent in non-interactive CI pipes → the existing non-TTY guard is the degradation path (IT-asserted).

### Security (remote `curl | sh` + typed secrets)
- Threat: the wizard collects a **provider API key**. Invariants: the key is read via `read -rs < /dev/tty` (never echoed), lands **only** in `~/.fah/config.yaml`, never appears in argv/`ps` output, transcripts, or logs; the config write keeps current file-mode behavior.
- The POSIX rewrite must not "simplify" hidden input into visible echo or pass the key through `printf` argv in a way `ps` can catch (assign via `read`, not `var=$(… key on the command line)`).
- Supply chain: served over HTTPS from fa1.dev; existing `check_install_pin.sh` / `installer_verify_selftest.sh` guards stay. Checksum infrastructure = separate card (out of scope).

## Freshness audit (fresh main `92e939246`, 2026-10-14)
The dialect bug is not the only problem — the wizard's data is stale. Verified against fresh main; all `site/` files are byte-identical to the generator output (no artifact drift), so every finding below lives in the **source** (`site/install-config.yaml` + template) and ships on every fresh download:

| Surface | Wizard offers | fa reality (origin/main) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | 5: openrouter, anthropic, google, openai, custom | **12** in `provider_catalog.dart`: + copilot, zai, kimi, codemie, dial, minimax, chatgpt, aiin | **stale** |
| Approval modes | 3: yolo, write, always-ask | **4**: + `autopilot` (`kAutopilotLabel`, formerly `unattended`) | **stale** |
| Model presets | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 (recommended)`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` | current catalog defaults | **stale** |
| Agent modes | code, architect, review | `builtInAgentModes` = default(code), architect, review | ✓ current |
| Config keys written | provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode/allowedTools | all live in `settings_registry` (`yamlKeys`) | ✓ current |
| Interactive stdin (`read < /dev/tty`), non-TTY guard | as designed | unchanged on main | ✓ current |

Provider surface is actively moving upstream (gh-1554 scoped timeouts, gh-1570 ProviderModelBinding) — another reason the wizard's provider data must be **generated from the live catalog**, not hand-maintained in yaml.

### Addition to the fix (same card)
- **AC6** — the wizard's provider list, approval-mode list, and model presets are **generated from `provider_catalog.dart`** (gen_installers reads the catalog or a checked-in snapshot with a drift test): provider menu names == catalog names, approval menu = always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot, presets = current recommended defaults. A catalog change without regeneration fails `UT-2` (golden drift, extended to the data sections).
- Provider menu ordering: keep openrouter first (recommended), then the rest by catalog order; `custom` stays last.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `site/setup.sh.template` contains zero POSIX-violating constructs (automated scan: `printf -v`, `[[`, `read -p`, arrays, `${var,,}`, `=~`); regenerated `site/setup.sh` identical to the scan-clean template. Hook: `gen_installers` golden test + a new template lint.
- **AC2** — Piped wizard (`curl -fsSL … | sh` equivalent: `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'`) with scripted `/dev/tty` answers picks Custom (option 5), accepts endpoint+key, writes a valid `~/.fah/config.yaml`, exits 0 — under **dash**, **busybox ash**, and **bash**. Hook: IT pty harness.
- **AC3** — The hidden API key never appears in the captured transcript of the IT runs (byte-scan the fixture for the key literal) and `~/.fah/config.yaml` contains it exactly once.
- **AC4** — Non-TTY run prints the existing clear guidance and exits non-zero without writing `.fah` (parity with today's guard).
- **AC5** — `bash site/setup.sh` (direct, non-piped) behavior is unchanged (existing UX preserved; no prompt-text drift).

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-1` — template lint: forbidden-construct scan (AC1). Pure grep/dart, no IO.
- `UT-2` — golden drift: emitted `site/setup.sh` == regeneration from template+yaml (AC1; extends the existing selftest).
- `IT-1` — dash pty run, full wizard, option 5 Custom, fixture config asserted (AC2, AC3).

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

blocks.text:
# gh-1596: [GOAL] POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard — setup.sh completes under curl | sh on dash/busybox/bash (fixes #1596 crash)

## Description

## Goal — POSIX-sh portable first-run wizard (v1, converted from bug report)
One sentence: **`curl -fsSL https://fa1.dev/setup.sh | sh` completes the full first-run wizard and writes a working `~/.fah/config.yaml` under every mainstream POSIX sh — dash, busybox ash, bash — not only bash.**

Today `site/setup.sh` is bash-only: 7 uses of the bash builtin `printf -v`. Under `curl | sh` the shebang is ignored — whatever `sh` resolves to executes the script — and on Ubuntu 24.04 (sh = dash) the wizard aborts at the first prompt: `printf: Illegal option -v`. `.fah` is never created. Reported by an external user (khoser); this is the first-run experience for every new Linux user.

## Why this framing
- The fix lands in the **generator pipeline**, not the artifact: `site/install-config.yaml` + `site/setup.sh.template` → `scripts/gen_installers.dart` → `site/setup.sh` (`DO NOT EDIT BY HAND` header). A hand-patch of `site/setup.sh` regresses on the next release.
- Retracted framing: "add/fix the bash shebang" — under `curl | sh` a shebang is dead text; the script must be valid for whatever shell the pipe feeds. Never revisit.
- The wizard's interactive-stdin design is already correct (`read … < /dev/tty`, non-TTY guard at the top) — this card changes **nothing** about the UX, only the shell dialect.

## Architecture
```
site/install-config.yaml ─┐
site/setup.sh.template ───┴─> scripts/gen_installers.dart ──> site/setup.sh  (curl | sh target)
                                                            └> site/install.sh, install.bat/ps1
```
Invariants:
- **I1 (dialect):** every `sh`-targeted emitted script parses and runs under dash, busybox ash, and bash. POSIX subset only: no `printf -v`, no `[[ ]]`, no arrays, no `local -a`, no `read -p/-a/-N`, no `${var,,}`, no `=~`.
- **I2 (single source):** emitted `site/setup.sh` is byte-identical to a fresh regeneration (existing pin/selftest guards keep enforcing this).
- **I3 (UX parity):** prompt texts, provider menu, hidden key entry (`read -rs < /dev/tty`), and the non-TTY degradation path behave identically on bash and dash.

## Capability surface (what the wizard must do → portability shape)
| Surface | Today | This card |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Prompt helpers (`ask`, `ask_hidden`, `confirm`) | `printf -v` assignment (bash-only) | POSIX assignment via command substitution (`var=$(…)`) with exit-code propagation |
| Interactive stdin | `read -r < /dev/tty` (correct) | unchanged |
| Non-TTY path | guard at line 143, clear message | unchanged + IT-covered |
| Config write | `~/.fah/config.yaml` | unchanged (E3 pins no-clobber) |
| CI portability guard | none | **core**: dash + busybox smoke jobs |
| `shellcheck --shell=sh` over emitted sh | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Non-interactive env setup (`FA_SETUP_PROVIDER=…`) | none | second tier (opt-in follow-up) |
| Rewrite wizard in another language / compiled helper | — | **excluded**: 400 lines of POSIX sh is the right tool; a binary bootstrap adds supply-chain surface for zero UX gain |
| Re-exec into bash from the piped script | — | **excluded**: impossible without writing a temp file from remote code — new attack surface; removing bashisms is strictly simpler |

### Platform facts (pinned, each with a test)
- **dash** (Ubuntu `sh`, Debian): `printf` has no `-v` → the #1596 crash. Negative test: dash run of the old script fails at line 74; positive: new script completes.
- **busybox ash** (Alpine, slim containers): same; also strict about `local` outside functions. Smoke-covered.
- **macOS `sh`** = bash 3.2 POSIX mode: *accepts* `printf -v` (bash builtin quirk) — that's why the bug never fired on macOS. Positive test only (no macOS regression possible from this fix).
- **`/dev/tty`** exists in interactive sessions, absent in non-interactive CI pipes → the existing non-TTY guard is the degradation path (IT-asserted).

### Security (remote `curl | sh` + typed secrets)
- Threat: the wizard collects a **provider API key**. Invariants: the key is read via `read -rs < /dev/tty` (never echoed), lands **only** in `~/.fah/config.yaml`, never appears in argv/`ps` output, transcripts, or logs; the config write keeps current file-mode behavior.
- The POSIX rewrite must not "simplify" hidden input into visible echo or pass the key through `printf` argv in a way `ps` can catch (assign via `read`, not `var=$(… key on the command line)`).
- Supply chain: served over HTTPS from fa1.dev; existing `check_install_pin.sh` / `installer_verify_selftest.sh` guards stay. Checksum infrastructure = separate card (out of scope).

## Freshness audit (fresh main `92e939246`, 2026-10-14)
The dialect bug is not the only problem — the wizard's data is stale. Verified against fresh main; all `site/` files are byte-identical to the generator output (no artifact drift), so every finding below lives in the **source** (`site/install-config.yaml` + template) and ships on every fresh download:

| Surface | Wizard offers | fa reality (origin/main) | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Providers | 5: openrouter, anthropic, google, openai, custom | **12** in `provider_catalog.dart`: + copilot, zai, kimi, codemie, dial, minimax, chatgpt, aiin | **stale** |
| Approval modes | 3: yolo, write, always-ask | **4**: + `autopilot` (`kAutopilotLabel`, formerly `unattended`) | **stale** |
| Model presets | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 (recommended)`, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, `claude-sonnet-4-5` | current catalog defaults | **stale** |
| Agent modes | code, architect, review | `builtInAgentModes` = default(code), architect, review | ✓ current |
| Config keys written | provider/model/baseUrl/mode/approvalMode/allowedTools | all live in `settings_registry` (`yamlKeys`) | ✓ current |
| Interactive stdin (`read < /dev/tty`), non-TTY guard | as designed | unchanged on main | ✓ current |

Provider surface is actively moving upstream (gh-1554 scoped timeouts, gh-1570 ProviderModelBinding) — another reason the wizard's provider data must be **generated from the live catalog**, not hand-maintained in yaml.

### Addition to the fix (same card)
- **AC6** — the wizard's provider list, approval-mode list, and model presets are **generated from `provider_catalog.dart`** (gen_installers reads the catalog or a checked-in snapshot with a drift test): provider menu names == catalog names, approval menu = always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot, presets = current recommended defaults. A catalog change without regeneration fails `UT-2` (golden drift, extended to the data sections).
- Provider menu ordering: keep openrouter first (recommended), then the rest by catalog order; `custom` stays last.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — `site/setup.sh.template` contains zero POSIX-violating constructs (automated scan: `printf -v`, `[[`, `read -p`, arrays, `${var,,}`, `=~`); regenerated `site/setup.sh` identical to the scan-clean template. Hook: `gen_installers` golden test + a new template lint.
- **AC2** — Piped wizard (`curl -fsSL … | sh` equivalent: `dash -c 'cat site/setup.sh | dash'`) with scripted `/dev/tty` answers picks Custom (option 5), accepts endpoint+key, writes a valid `~/.fah/config.yaml`, exits 0 — under **dash**, **busybox ash**, and **bash**. Hook: IT pty harness.
- **AC3** — The hidden API key never appears in the captured transcript of the IT runs (byte-scan the fixture for the key literal) and `~/.fah/config.yaml` contains it exactly once.
- **AC4** — Non-TTY run prints the existing clear guidance and exits non-zero without writing `.fah` (parity with today's guard).
- **AC5** — `bash site/setup.sh` (direct, non-piped) behavior is unchanged (existing UX preserved; no prompt-text drift).

## Test plan
### Test matrix
- `UT-1` — template lint: forbidden-construct scan (AC1). Pure grep/dart, no IO.
- `UT-2` — golden drift: emitted `site/setup.sh` == regeneration from template+yaml (AC1; extends the existing selftest).
- `IT-1` — dash pty run, full wizard, option 5 Custom, fixture config asserted (AC2, AC3).
- `IT-2` — busybox ash pty run, same fixture (AC2).
- `IT-3`…

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \

      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared changes — shard green-skipped (required context reported)"

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

    name: Hostile ambient env

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \

      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).

- uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
      - name: dart analyze (full)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart analyze

      - name: dart analyze (docs-only scope)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true'
        run: dart analyze lib test bin

      # Publish gate at PR time: publish-blocking problems (undeclared lib/
      # imports, stray PEM-like strings) used to surface only in the tag-time
      # publish job — the v0.1.331 era: an undeclared package:cryptography
      # import shipped red on ~26 consecutive tags. --ignore-warnings: the
      # two known layout warnings (gitignored install_local.sh, docs/
      # naming) must not redden every PR, while validation ERRORS — "does
      # not have X in the dependencies section of pubspec.yaml" — still
      # fail. setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) registers a publish-scoped PUB_TOKEN
      # job-wide and pub.dev rejects authenticated metadata reads, so
      # resolve unauthenticated (same pattern as the publish job);
      # --dry-run never uploads.
      - name: Publish dry-run (unauthenticated)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true
          # Against the STAGED tree, not the repo root (#597 AC1): the
          # publish job publishes from the stage — the v0.1.407 class of
          # failure (staged resolution re-pinning vendor/dart_tui through
          # pubspec_overrides.yaml) must redden the PR, not the tag.
          bash scripts/stage_publish_package.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage
          # gh-1538: the STAMP rehearsal moved here from the retired nightly
          # full-quality leg — the pre-merge gate is the single test gate
          # now, so a stamp failure (placeholder leak, changelog-section
          # generation, staged-version desync, cap trim) must redden the
          # PR, not surface at tag time. Rehearses the NEXT tag's payload
          # exactly like the nightly leg did (gh-1522).
          latest=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1)
          latest="${latest#v}"
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$latest"
          next="$major.$minor.$((patch + 1))"
          echo "rehearsing the stamp of the NEXT tag: v$next"
          bash scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage "$next"
          # The staged tree must ANALYZE clean: v0.1.411 shipped files
          # with broken imports (the staging filter pruned lib/src/memory;
          # imports of fork-only dart_tui symbols) that only a consumer's
          # `dart analyze` ever surfaced (issue #613). Errors fail the
          # gate; warnings/infos pass, matching the static analyze stage.
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub get && dart analyze)
          (cd /tmp/pr-dry-run-stage && dart pub publish --dry-run --ignore-warnings)

  test-core:
    # Always runs (no job-level path gate): a path-filtered matrix skip
    # posts a check-run with the LITERAL unrendered name — the required
    # contexts (shard 0..3) never report, and branch protection blocks
    # out-of-scope PRs at 27 green checks. The scope fastpass below
    # green-skips the real steps in seconds instead.
    name: Core tests (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    timeout-minutes: 12

sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

# ambient-env read that leaks back into resolution regresses loudly.
  # gh-1198 rework: the runner now ALSO exports FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE (the
  # provider-queue env won over the file queue and silently flipped the
  # /providers queue editor tests to the env-wins refusal on the PR head) —
  # the var rides the same hostile block so a future ambient read of it
  # regresses here, not only on the runner.
  hostile-env:
    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    if: (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true') && needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py \
            test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json \
            test-results/junit-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml

      # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites
      # are integration-tagged (the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
      # lib/src/cli hits from them), so the sharded unit run above skips
      # them. Their hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers
      # (>= 80% ratchet, PR diff-coverage, CRAP — jsr_cli.dart at 0% reads
      # CRAP 156 > 12), so they run into shard 0's coverage dir; the gate
      # merge is a union, so one shard carrying them is enough. Keep this
      # list in sync with scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_test_core (gh-1538
      # retired the nightly full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the
      # single unit-lcov producer now).
      - name: dart test --tags integration (jsr delegate trio → unit lcov)
        if: matrix.shard == 0 && (needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true')

    name: Hostile ambient env
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do

            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)

                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this

#   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
          #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
          #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
          #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
          #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
          #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
          #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
          #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
          #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
          #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).
          platform_red=false
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "usage-fold:$R_USAGE_FOLD" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "fa-aot-build:$R_FA_AOT" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-portability:$R_INSTALLER_REG" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE" \
                    "flutter-app-exzone:$R_EXZONE" "flutter-app-lock-smoke:$R_LOCK_SMOKE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            case "$name" in
              build-web|build-android|build-ios|build-macos|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
                  platform_red=true
                fi
                ;;
              *)
                if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ] && [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
                  dart_blocker="a leg is $r ($name)"
                fi
                ;;
            esac
          done
          if [ -n "$dart_blocker" ]; then dart_ok=false; else dart_ok=true; fi
          echo "dart_ok=$dart_ok" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Aggregate verdicts AFTER the export — branch protection is
          # unchanged: ANY red leg (package or platform) still fails this
          # required check; only the PUBLISH gate ignores platform reds.
          [ -z "$dart_blocker" ] || fail "$dart_blocker"
          [ "$platform_red" = "false" ] || fail "a platform/native leg is red — the aggregate is red; dart_ok stays true (publish is not gated on platform legs, #1368), see the leg results above"
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, changes]
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read

Now I see the mismatch:

- ci.yml line 3012: `...|flutter-app-lock-smoke|installer-portability)` — the PR appended `installer-portability` at the END of the case pattern.
- The test expects the pattern `...|fa-aot-build|installer-verify|install-pin-gate|cube-kernel-live|cli-visual-settings|pty-integration-linux|pty-coverage-gate|pty-visual|flutter-app-lock-smoke)` — with `installer-portability` NOT in it at all, and ending with `flutter-app-lock-smoke)`.

The PR's choice of appending `|installer-portability` at the end broke the test's `contains` check since the test pins the exact verbatim pattern ending `flutter-app-lock-smoke)`.

Interesting design question: is `installer-portability` a "platform" leg or a "dart/package" leg?

Looking at the classification: `installer-portability` runs `dart test` — it's actually a Dart test leg (UT/IT of the installer). But its matrix is ubuntu+macos... Hmm. The PR treats it as a platform leg (platform_red only), meaning a red installer-portability leg blocks the merge via the aggregate but doesn't gate dart_ok (the publish). But the ticket says:

> **REG-1** — CI job (ubuntu) runs IT-1, IT-2, UT-1 on every PR touching `site/` or `scripts/gen_installers.dart`. **A red REG job blocks merge even when everything else is green.**

And the PR description says: "red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class". So the PR's intent: `installer-portability` is classified as a platform leg → `platform_red` → blocks merge (aggregate red) but not publish (dart_ok).

Now the test `#1368: quality-gate exports dart_ok; platform legs cannot redden it` pins the verbatim case pattern ending with `flutter-app-lock-smoke)`. The PR changed the pattern, breaking the pin.

Two options to fix:
1. Update the test to include `installer-portability` in the expected verbatim pattern (test change).
2. Change ci.yml to keep the old pattern intact and classify `installer-portability` differently.

Which is right? The test's stated reason: "every platform/native/PTY leg must be publish-exempt — flutter-app-lock-smoke included (#1267 N2: a red lockfile smoke release build blocks the merge via the aggregate, never the publish)".

`installer-portability` is a REG (regression) leg running Dart tests on the installer shell artifacts. It's essentially a test leg — arguably a dart/package leg. Hmm, but its purpose per the PR: "red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class."

Wait — actually, let me re-read the PR description: "New REG CI leg `installer-portability` (path-triggered on `site/**` + the generator): ubuntu runs dash + busybox ash, macOS runs bash; red blocks the merge via the quality-gate platform class."

So the PR deliberately classified it as platform. The question is whether that's the right class:
- platform legs are native/PTY builds that can be flaky/environment-shaped and shouldn't block the pure-Dart publish.
- installer-portability runs dart tests that spawn shell processes — they're hermetic-ish but depend on shell availability; skipped when shells are absent... Actually the leg installs dash+busybox on ubuntu explicitly, so it's deterministic there.

Is it more consistent to make it a package/dart leg (dart_blocker)? The ticket says a red REG job blocks merge even when everything else is green — both classes do that (both fail the aggregate). The difference is only whether it also reds dart_ok (blocks publish).

Hmm, but consider: the installer-portability leg is about the shell wizard, not the Dart package. A red here doesn't mean the Dart package is broken — the published package doesn't contain site/setup.sh. So platform class is right — publish-exempt. The PR's own test `ci_1596_installer_portability_ci_test.dart` asserts: "quality-gate needs the leg, consumes its result, classifies it" — let me check what that test asserts exactly.

Also the review thread 0 — no open threads. The failing tests are what I must fix.
